title: Benchmark identity, comparison, SLO, offload, and client workflows

sources.notes: Models positional comparison and missing provenance gate. run_config names absent benchmarks/benchmark.py; capacity consumption also disagrees with the current nested producer schema.

Maps stored measurements to markdown. Row-order concurrency, nominal context equivalence, missing-data tolerance, and same-checkpoint language are assumptions/inferences rather than validated identity.
Top-level shell observer has no named functions. It counts report.json rather than successful manifests and probes fixed port 8017; observations are advisory.
Primary canonical identity, manifest, resume, command, cell execution, result, and failure source. Completion is exact integer return_code zero; a report is not required.
Restarts by context but reuses one identity directory while context belongs to identity. Runner failures and low-memory observations do not prevent the final done banner.
Models construction-time all-CUDA, hybrid, and all-out modes plus measured versus derived evidence. Source digest path and environment sanitation omissions are retained as provenance limits.
Informational reducer. Baseline is inferred from zero B70 share, identity is unchecked, and CPU route/service attribution is absent.
Pairwise deterministic provider-output byte gate. The header's A1/A2 nondeterminism envelope is not implemented or modeled as fact.
Models prefix-cache cold/repeat passes, evidence collection, warnings, and weak resume identity. Cold does not denote the CPU expert tier.
Historical top-level shell orchestration has no named functions. Warm/PSI handling and skip-existing evidence are described; config equivalence is not hashed.
Historical top-level shell orchestration has no named functions. Selected-cell deletion, nonfatal spot checks, and presence-based completion are inventory contracts, not measured claims.
Top-level shell entry has no named functions. Its per-cell invocations conflict with whole-run identity because contexts/profiles change at one model directory.
Fresh subprocess per arm; CPU all-out and streaming placements are opt-in. Existing pathname alone is treated as reusable evidence.
Models custom XML, sequential tool results, normal-result error channel, raw XML history, context retry, and the 20-generation bound. Tool payload bytes and filesystem side effects are abstract.
Models readiness, command/turn loop, permissive EOF, server-usage accounting, pending-user rollback, and exclusion of reasoning from history.
Primary continuous-usage request validity and aggregation contract. It measures SLO-relevant metrics but contains no numeric SLO pass/fail policy.
Models serial fresh engines and dispatch/stream/all-out branches at the benchmark lifecycle level. Appended suffixes do not establish prefix-cache invalidation.
Top-level shell launcher has no named functions. One Python process constructs several engines; explicit-empty MODES is an argparse error, not an empty sweep.
Watcher/audit/teardown/Track-B composition. External chain_audit owns the gate; watched-process status is unavailable and persistent/unreadable B70 residency can still proceed.
Post-hoc/preemptive addressing comparison with explicitly accepted activation/fold differences. Output wording is narrower than literal all-field identity and capture provenance is incomplete.
Executable source contract for matrix identity/resume, read but not run here. It does not integration-test the shell wrappers' fragmented invocations.

assumptions: Positive bounded integers abstract canonical JSON SHA-256 identities; collision resistance and filesystem bytes are outside the model.
One subprocess, cold/warm pass, engine arm, SSE delivery, or agent model-plus-tool round is atomic at its stated boundary.
Measured evidence is distinct from source-derived summaries and inferred/manual classifications; no latency or speed claim is introduced.
Matrix return_code zero means resumable completion exactly as implemented, not result-file validity or SLO success.
Cold/warm denotes prefix-cache state; AllOut denotes the optional CPU/DRAM expert tier.
Interactive EOF acceptance is preserved even though DONE and finish_reason are not validated.
GuideLLM, vLLM, model/tokenizer checkpoints, plugin/provider libraries, hardware runtimes, Prometheus, native traces, and external result trees remain dependency boundaries.

implementation_checks.description: CPU-only differential: construct two RunConfig values and canonical server-manifest objects to show excluded operational paths preserve identity while workload/server-content changes alter it.
CPU-only temporary-directory differential: exercise rc 0, nonzero, null, malformed, mismatched, and orphan manifests and compare returned completed-cell sets or rejection without overwrite.
CPU-only pure-data comparison: feed successful, failed, and bundled-delivery result dictionaries and verify measurement availability and missing ITL remain distinct from numeric SLO judgment.
CPU-only differential over token lists for exact, partial-prefix, and empty outputs; separately inspect that compare_correctness reports rather than rejects divergence.
CPU-only NPZ differential: compare identical arrays, differing cell sets, and one-element byte changes to establish the implemented pairwise gate without asserting the unimplemented envelope.
CPU-only JSONL differential: vary addressing digests, activation/fold fields, alpha ratios, missing vectors, and duplicate layers to characterize the actual accepted classification.
CPU-only parser comparison for multiple calls, repeated parameters, coercible and non-coercible scalars, unknown parameters, and incomplete XML.

Source inspection comparison of effective environment for AllCuda, Hybrid, and AllOut, including inherited PREEMPTIVE_SURGERY; a real CPU-tier performance comparison still requires the configured server hardware and must bind full identity.
